title: The bounded Grassmannian rank stratum classifies projective closed families
statement: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a Noetherian commutative ring $A$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum], $n\geq0$, and $E\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_U$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-projective]. Fix a numerical polynomial $P$ [def-sfb-projective-fibre-hilbert-polynomial]. Fix $m\geq1$ satisfying the following uniform bound for every scheme $T$: if $Z\subset\mathbf P^n_T$ is flat and finitely presented over $T$ with fibre polynomial $P$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], writing $q:Z\to T$, $p:\mathbf P^n_T\to T$, $V_{d,T}=\mathcal O_T[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_d$ and $\mathcal I_Z$ for its ideal, then for $d\geq m$ the restriction sequence $0\to p_*\mathcal I_Z(d)\to V_{d,T}\to q_*\mathcal O_Z(d)\to0$ has finite locally free terms and last rank $P(d)$, commutes with arbitrary base change, and both evaluation from $p_*\mathcal I_Z(m)$ and multiplication $V_{d-m,T}\otimes p_*\mathcal I_Z(m)\to p_*\mathcal I_Z(d)$ are surjective. Twists are those of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]; finite locally free means locally a finite direct sum of copies of the structure sheaf. Suppose $P(d)\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ for $d\geq m$ and $r=P(m)\leq N=\binom{n+m}{n}$. Let $G=G_U(N,r)$ be the free-quotient Grassmannian with universal kernel $R_m\subset V_{m,G}$ [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective]. Let $I_E\subset A[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ be the homogeneous ideal of polynomials restricting to zero on $E$, with $E=\operatorname{Proj}(A[x]/I_E)$ [def-pc-proj]. Put $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_G[x_0,\ldots,x_n]/(I_E,R_m)$, where the first ideal is extended coefficientwise and the second is generated in degree $m$ [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. There is a finite-type immersion $j:Y\to G$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] such that an arbitrary $g:T\to G$ factors uniquely through $Y$ exactly when $g^*\mathcal B_d$ is locally free of rank $P(d)$ for all $d\geq m$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. The family $\operatorname{Proj}_Y(\mathcal B|_Y)\subset E_Y$ [def-nagata-relative-proj, def-pc-fibre-product] induces a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_U(T,Y)\cong\{Z\subset E_T:Z/T\text{ flat and finitely presented with fibre polynomial }P\}$ [def-pc-representable-functor]. Its inverse sends $Z$ to the quotient $V_{m,T}\twoheadrightarrow q_*\mathcal O_Z(m)$. These are inverse as closed subschemes and quotient maps, also for nonreduced and non-Noetherian $T$, and commute with arbitrary pullback of test schemes. No flatness of $E/U$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 2.1 (boundedness), and Lemmas 3.3--3.4, printed pp.261--264: bounded-degree Grassmannian quotient, graded rank locus and the two inverse transformations; Remark 3.9, p.266. Modern finitely presented formulation on arbitrary test schemes. Archival PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: The Grassmannian $G\to U$ is H-projective by [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective], hence proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $U$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $G$ Noetherian. For an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset G$, [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes $C$ Noetherian and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $C[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ Noetherian. The quotient $\mathcal B$ is quasi-coherent degreewise: locally split the universal quotient by lifting a frame of its locally free target. Its kernel $R_m$ is then a direct summand of $V_m$. The equations from $I_E$ and $R_m$, their polynomial multiples and their images commute with localization on $W$. Their degree-$d$ image is therefore a quasi-coherent submodule of $V_d$, and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] identifies the quotient with $\mathcal B_d$. The ideal of equations on $W$ is finitely generated, with homogeneous generators: replace any finite generating set by all its homogeneous components. These assertions also hold when the ideal contains degree-zero elements.

source.place: Tags 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); algebra.tex Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); schemes.tex Tag 01IC (quasi-coherent cokernels).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-graded-tail-rank-stratum] over $G$, taking its algebra to be $\mathcal S=\mathcal O_G[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ and its graded module to be $M=\mathcal B$. Here $\mathcal S_0=\mathcal O_G$, its degree-one part is finite free and generates it, and $\mathcal B$ is generated as an $\mathcal S$-module by $1$ (or by the empty family if it is zero). Step 1 verifies quasi-coherence and Noetherianity; the assumed nonnegative integral values of $P(d)$ verify the rank hypotheses. This gives exactly a finite-type immersion $j:Y\to G$ with the asserted unique factorization property for every scheme $T$. Taking the polynomial algebra, rather than $\mathcal B$, as the algebra in that lemma avoids any assumption that $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_G$. The identity of $Y$ satisfies the rank conditions, so every $\mathcal B_d|_Y$ is locally free of rank $P(d)$ for $d\geq m$. Also $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

source.place: Lemma 3.4, printed pp.262--264; the polynomial-algebra/module formulation includes degree-zero equations.

proof.text: The pullback of the equations to $Y$ is again a locally finitely generated homogeneous ideal: this follows either by pulling back the finite local generating lists of Step 1 or by Noetherianity on affine opens of $Y$. Thus [lem-sfb-flat-graded-tail-proj] applies over the Noetherian scheme $Y$ to $\mathcal B|_Y$. It gives a closed subscheme $Z_Y=\operatorname{Proj}_Y(\mathcal B|_Y)\subset\mathbf P^n_Y$, flat and finitely presented over $Y$, with fibre polynomial $P$. It also identifies the coefficientwise pullbacks with the base-changed closed subscheme. Since the quotient algebra kills $I_E$, its surjection factors through $\mathcal O_Y[x]/(I_E)$. The surjective-map clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] gives a closed immersion into $\operatorname{Proj}_Y(\mathcal O_Y[x]/(I_E))$. By [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] and the given presentation of $E$, the latter is $E_Y$, with its specified projective embedding. Hence this is a family inside $E_Y$, with no flatness assumption on $E/U$.

For $h:T\to Y$, pull back $Z_Y$ as a closed subscheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], it is flat and finitely presented over $T$. By [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality], its fibre polynomial is still $P$. The pullback assertion of [lem-sfb-flat-graded-tail-proj] identifies it, including its equations and embedding, with $\operatorname{Proj}_T(g^*\mathcal B)$, where $g=jh$. In particular this construction works for non-Noetherian $T$. For any $g:T\to G$, ordinary pullback is tensor pullback by [def-pc-module-pullback], and
$$g^*\mathcal B=\mathcal O_T[x_0,\ldots,x_n]/(I_E,R_{m,T}),\qquad R_{m,T}=g^*R_m.$$
Indeed locally maps from either algebra into an $\mathcal O_T$-algebra are choices of the coordinate images annihilating the images of exactly these equations. This verifies the quotient identity without treating a pulled-back ideal as an injected submodule. The pulled-back universal kernel does inject into $V_{m,T}$ because its sequence is locally split.

Conversely let $Z\subset E_T$ be any family in the statement and put $K_d=p_*\mathcal I_Z(d)$ and $E_d=q_*\mathcal O_Z(d)$. The assumed uniform bound gives $V_{m,T}\twoheadrightarrow E_m$, with $E_m$ locally free of rank $r$; [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective] gives its unique classifying map $g_Z:T\to G$. The pulled-back universal sequence is locally split, so its kernel is exactly $R_{m,T}=K_m$. Put $J_T=(I_E,K_m)\subset\mathcal O_T[x]$. Every equation in $I_E$ restricts to zero on $Z$, including after nonflat base change, since $Z\subset E_T$. For $d\geq m$, the multiplication hypothesis says that the image of $V_{d-m,T}\otimes K_m$ in $V_{d,T}$ is $K_d$. This image is contained in $(J_T)_d$, while every generator of $J_T$, and hence every polynomial multiple, restricts to zero on $Z$. Thus $(J_T)_d=K_d$ as sheaf submodules of $V_{d,T}$. Taking the quotient in the assumed restriction sequence and using Step 4 gives $g_Z^*\mathcal B_d=V_{d,T}/K_d\cong E_d$ for every $d\geq m$. These are locally free of rank $P(d)$, so Step 2 supplies a unique $h_Z:T\to Y$ with $jh_Z=g_Z$.

source.place: Lemma 3.3, necessity of the graded rank condition and the degree-m Grassmannian map; the uniform generation hypotheses are assumptions of this item.

proof.text: The family attached to $h_Z$ is $Z$ as a closed subscheme. To check its ideal, work over an affine open of $T$ and on a standard chart $D_+(x_i)$ of projective space, as supplied by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. By [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison], the chart of the quotient Proj is obtained by sending $a/x_i^e$ to its image in the quotient's degree-zero localization, and a degree-$m$ equation $a$ has local equation $a/x_i^m$. Thus the ideal generated on this chart by $K_m$ is exactly the image of the evaluation map $p^*K_m\otimes\mathcal O(-m)\to\mathcal I_Z$. This map is surjective by hypothesis, so that image is $\mathcal I_Z$. The additional equations from $I_E$ already belong to $\mathcal I_Z$. Therefore the chart quotient ideals defining $\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal O_T[x]/J_T)$ and $Z$ agree. The standard charts cover, so their ideal sheaves, and hence the closed subschemes with their embeddings in $E_T$, agree. This uses the evaluation hypothesis, not equality of underlying point sets or a saturation assumption.

source.place: Tag 07ZK (lemma-surjective-generated-degree-1-map-relative-proj) and Tag 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves); degree-m evaluation on the standard charts, spelling out Expose 221 Lemma 3.3.

proof.text:
Start instead with $h:T\to Y$ and its family $Z_h$. Step 4 makes this a family to which the uniform bound applies. Write $Q_T=V_{m,T}/R_{m,T}$ for the quotient classified by $g=jh$. All equations from $R_{m,T}$ vanish on $Z_h$: on the standard charts their restrictions are precisely the quotient-ring images of the same polynomials, by [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison]. Consequently restriction factors as
$$V_{m,T}\twoheadrightarrow Q_T\xrightarrow{\alpha}q_*\mathcal O_{Z_h}(m).$$
The composite is surjective by the uniform bound, so $\alpha$ is surjective. Both its source and target are locally free of rank $r$. On local frames its residue matrix is a surjective square matrix over a field, hence its determinant is a unit at every stalk. The adjugate identity [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] gives a local inverse, and uniqueness glues these inverses. Thus $\alpha$ is an isomorphism respecting the displayed quotient maps. The Grassmannian classifying map recovered from $Z_h$ is exactly $g$ by [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective], and its factorization through $Y$ is exactly $h$ by Step 2. The argument includes rank zero and does not require the base to be reduced.

source.place: Lemma 3.3, printed p.262: the natural surjection between locally free modules of the same rank is an isomorphism; algebra.tex Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse), adjugate identity.

proof.text: Steps 6 and 7 prove that the two assignments are inverse, both on embedded closed subschemes and on the quotient classes defining Grassmannian points. For a test morphism $a:T'\to T$, the forward quotient of a family pulls back to its quotient on $T'$ by the arbitrary-base-change clause of the assumed uniform bound. The Grassmannian universal property in [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective] therefore identifies its classifying map with $g_Za$; uniqueness in Step 2 identifies its lift with $h_Za$. In the other direction, the pullback clause of [lem-sfb-flat-graded-tail-proj] identifies the family of $ha$ with $(Z_h)_{T'}$, including its equations. These are the required naturality identities. All local computations used sheaf ideals or quotient maps, and all base changes were arbitrary; neither reducedness nor Noetherianity of $T$ entered. Empty test schemes give the unique empty family and unique maps, so are included as well.
